Lead profile: SMB, mid-growth support SaaS. Self-serve signup last week; technical discovery call 2026-03-01. Primary contact: CTO Elena Martinez (hands-on, cares about uptime). Product lead: Sam Ortiz. Wants hosted API — quick onramp and simple quota controls.

Key ask: robust guidance / POC for rate-limits, quotas, and burst handling. They get highly bursty traffic (chat widgets + inbound email triage) — short spikes of 200–300 requests within 30–90s windows when a campaign hits. Typical baseline: 5–10 req/s; peak bursts 150–300 req/s for 1–3 minutes. Concern: 429s during spikes => bad UX and customer complaints. Quote from CTO: "We can tolerate occasional 429s for non-critical flows but can't have sustained 429s for chat sessions — must degrade gracefully."

Desired behavior and asks: simple per-api-key concurrency limits, per-minute token quotas, a small burst buffer for short spikes, clear RateLimit headers and Retry-After, example client retry/backoff patterns, and dashboard visibility for spikes. Also interested in token-level cost hints in Console to estimate ARR impact of burst traffic. They prefer public cloud (no VPC for now) and want self-serve sandbox to validate.

Technical constraints: budget-conscious SMB. Latency target: 95th < 600ms for short chat responses (~150 tokens). Throughput target: sustain 30 req/s for steady peak, allow bursts to 200 req/s for up to 2 minutes. Cost sensitivity: high — want guidance on batching, streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, and suggested small-model fallbacks for non-critical paths.

Security/compliance notes: SSO for admin console and audit logs required. Legal raised a question about retention controls but not blocking for hosted API.
